channel.description: Latest articles from The College Fix (thecollegefix.com)

item.title: Intersectional conundrum: Palestinian watermelon mural upsets black community
item.description: A pro-Palestinian mural in Richmond featuring a watermelon has sparked controversy in the black community, with leaders expressing concerns over its historical connotations. While the mural symbolizes Palestinian identity, some feel it unintentionally invokes stereotypes. Activists suggest modifications to bridge solidarity between the black liberation and Palestinian movements, emphasizing unity in their struggles.

item.title: Teacher forced to resign for refusing to use ‘preferred pronouns’ gets $650,000 settlement
item.description: An Indiana music teacher, John Kluge, received a $650,000 settlement after being forced to resign for not using students' preferred pronouns. The court ruled public schools cannot compel teachers to compromise their religious beliefs, noting employers must accommodate them. This case highlights the potential legal and financial consequences of ignoring such accommodations in schools.

item.title: Stanford student gov. wants reinstatement of student co-ops suspended for antisemitic, anti-white actions
item.description: The Stanford Undergraduate Senate has passed a bill advocating for the reinstatement of two suspended student co-ops, following complaints about antisemitic and anti-white actions. The co-ops argue they provide valuable community spaces, including communal kitchens, and claim their suspension has disrupted operations and student well-being.

item.title: Virginia bill would mandate teaching of Jan. 6, 2021 as an ‘insurrection’
item.description: Virginia's legislature passed a bill mandating the teaching of January 6, 2021, as an "insurrection," prohibiting alternative descriptions. Critics argue it undermines academic freedom and enforces a partisan narrative, with the bill awaiting Governor Spanberger's signature. This move coincides with broader Democratic efforts to solidify their political agenda in the state.

item.title: Elementary school teacher suspended for telling kids they were ‘acting like monkeys in a zoo’
item.description: An Indiana elementary school teacher was suspended for telling his class they were "acting like monkeys in a zoo." The remarks, which drew immediate backlash, were reported by students. The school's administration is investigating, facing criticism from parents and community leaders for not addressing the issue promptly. The teacher claimed no racial intent.

item.title: Indiana U. Muslims upset at random ‘Islamophobic’ X post, inaction by school officials
item.description: Muslim students at Indiana University expressed their disappointment over a social media post deemed Islamophobic, highlighting a lack of administrative acknowledgment of their experiences. They seek more recognition and support as their community grows, with calls for additional prayer spaces on campus and an emphasis on the need for attentiveness to their concerns.

item.title: Classical Learning Test expands to more than 300 schools as alternative to SAT, ACT
item.description: The Classical Learning Test is being embraced by more states and universities, offering an alternative to traditional college admissions tests like the SAT and ACT.

item.title: Purdue seeks foreign worker to coach tennis
item.description: Purdue University looks outside of the United States to find an assistant women's tennis coach.

item.title: Catholic U. denies pro-Israel student group’s speakers, citing ‘lack of balance’
item.description: Catholic University of America denied speaker requests from the Students Supporting Israel chapter on campus, citing a lack of balance in viewpoints offered. The university told The College Fix it invited the students to resubmit their proposal with broader viewpoints. item.title: Princeton might start proctoring exams again for first time in over a century
item.description: Such a move would buck 133 years of precedent and 'would mark a departure from the traditionally unproctored exam format under the Honor Code.'
